papers.title_en: Symbolic Attack Chain Generation from Atomic Red Team Techniques: An Empirical Study of Predicate Representation Granularity
papers.evidence: 使用LLM将攻击技术转化为符号谓词，实现自动化攻击链生成，探索LLM在网络攻击规划中的能力
papers.tldr: 攻击链自动化生成对现代网络安全至关重要，而基于PDDL的AI规划方法依赖谓词表示粒度。现有九类AALM粒度必要性未经实证。本研究使用LLM转换技术，通过Fast Downward比较9类与5类粒度方案，发现有效性对粒度不敏感，81.3%结果一致。这表明高粒度主要提升计划依据的结构分辨率，而非攻击链可行性。
papers.abstract_en: Automated attack chain generation is critical for modern cybersecurity, yet manual construction fails to scale as adversary behaviors expand. While classical AI planning using PDDL offers a formal method to automate this process, it relies on the accurate translation of techniques into symbolic predicates. Current state-of-the-art systems like AURORA employ a nine-category Attack Action Linking Model (AALM), but the necessity of this specific granularity remains unvalidated. This work investigates the impact of predicate representation granularity on plan validity, cost, and fidelity. Utilizing a pipeline where a Large Language Model (LLM) performs translation and the Fast Downward engine performs deterministic reasoning, the study compares the full nine-category AALM against a reduced five-category scheme derived empirically from Atomic Red Team (ART) execution evidence. Results from a sixteen-technique corpus demonstrate that plan validity and cost are largely insensitive to granularity, with 81.3% identical outcomes across both schemes. The findings suggest that higher granularity primarily enhances the internal structural resolution of a plan's justification rather than the viability of the generated attack chain itself.

papers.title_en: LoginTrap: Uncovering Task-Agnostic Phishing-Style Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks against LLM-based Web Agents
papers.authors: Longtao Guo, Zelin Zhang, Kaifeng Huang, Yang Shi
papers.evidence: 诱导LLM网络智能体泄露登录凭据的钓鱼式攻击
papers.tldr: 基于LLM的Web Agent自动执行任务，登录成为敏感认证边界，恶意网页可能诱导登录并泄露私密数据。为此提出LoginTrap，一种任务无关的钓鱼式间接提示注入攻击，通过模糊测试生成页面特定注入，将登录伪装成任务先决条件，引导Agent进入攻击者控制的登录页面。实验显示，LoginTrap平均攻击成功率达86%，且跨不同LLM骨干、Agent架构和防御均保持有效。该研究系统揭示了登录诱导作为认证边界风险，为设计认证感知防御提供重要动机。
papers.abstract_en: LLM-based web agents automate user tasks by observing webpages and executing browser actions on behalf of users. As these agents operate on real web services, login becomes a sensitive authentication boundary because it involves credentials and sensitive information. Existing work shows that malicious webpage content can manipulate web agent actions, but it has not fully examined whether such content can induce login and cause end-to-end private data leakage. We study this attack surface and present LoginTrap, a task-agnostic login-inducing attack against LLM-based web agents. LoginTrap assumes a black box attacker that controls the webpage context and the induced login flow without knowing the user task or web agent internals. Under this threat model, LoginTrap uses webpage context to generate page-specific indirect injections through a fuzzing-inspired process, making login appear as a plausible prerequisite for continuing the task and guiding the agent to a controlled login page. We conduct a comprehensive analysis of LoginTrap across realistic web agent executions. The results show that LoginTrap reaches 86\% average end-to-end attack success across LLM backbones and remains effective across agent architectures and defenses. These findings identify login inducement as a systematic authentication boundary risk and motivate further research on authentication-aware defenses for web agents.

papers.title_en: Salami Attack: Stealthy Collusive Memory Poisoning against OpenClaw
papers.authors: Zheng Lin, Yuzhe Huang, Zhenxing Niu, Xianmin Ye, Haichang Gao
papers.evidence: 用于共谋记忆投毒的自动红队框架，测试LLM智能体漏洞
papers.tldr: 大型语言模型代理的持久记忆易受投毒攻击，现有方法仅关注单条恶意记录，忽视多条良性记忆的合谋威胁。本文提出MemCollusion，采萨拉米策略将攻击意图切分为无害片段，通过四项约束、五种策略及微调生成器构建记忆联盟，使记忆单独安全，组合有害。在仿真平台MoltLab上，48场景下最强模式中，记忆保存率81.3%，攻击成功率75.0%，并抗稀释和防御。该工作首次系统揭示合谋内存投毒风险，并提供了自动化红队评测工具，对LLM代理安全部署具重要价值。
papers.abstract_en: Long-term memory enables LLM agents to retain useful information across sessions, but also creates an attack surface through which adversaries may poison an agent's persistent memory to steer its behavior. Existing memory poisoning attacks mainly rely on individually malicious records, overlooking a compositional threat: multiple benign-looking memories may jointly induce unsafe behavior. In this paper, we introduce MemCollusion, an automated red-teaming framework for constructing collusive memory poisoning attacks. MemCollusion applies salami tactics---a strategy that slices an adversarial objective into small, individually innocuous pieces---to generate memory fragments that are individually benign looking but collectively harmful. It constructs memory coalitions using four design constraints, five theory-informed strategies, and a fine-tuned generator. To assess collusive memory poisoning in a realistic cross-session setting, we develop MoltLab, a controlled research reproduction of Moltbook, in which crafted platform content must first be observed and distilled into persistent memory before influencing the agent's behavior in a separate session. We evaluate MemCollusion on OpenClaw using two backbone models across 48 scenarios. Under the strongest memory-saving setting, MemCollusion achieves an average Memory Save Rate of 81.3% and an Attack Success Rate of 75.0%, and remains effective under both benign memory dilution and memory-level defenses.
